अरस्तू का दृष्टिकोण था कि किसी वस्तु को गतिमान रखने के लिए निरंतर बाह्य बल की आवश्यकता होती है। वे घर्षण जैसे विरोधी बलों की उपस्थिति के कारण इस निष्कर्ष पर पहुंचे थे। अतः यह कहना कि अरस्तू ने गति के लिए शून्य बल की अवधारणा दी थी, ऐतिहासिक एवं वैज्ञानिक दृष्टि से असत्य है।

अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: विरामावस्था और एकसमान गति की समतुल्यता से संबंधित पहला कथन सही है, जबकि अरस्तू की यांत्रिकी से संबंधित दूसरा कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS_11_LAWS_OF_MOTION_STATEMENT_Q02 - Nature and simultaneous action of third law forces

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Action and reaction forces in Newton's third law act simultaneously on two different bodies and never on the same body.

Statement II: There is no cause-and-effect relationship implied between action and reaction forces; either force may be designated as the action and the other as the reaction.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: न्यूटन के तीसरे नियम में क्रिया और प्रतिक्रिया बल दो अलग-अलग वस्तुओं पर एक साथ कार्य करते हैं और कभी भी एक ही वस्तु पर कार्य नहीं करते हैं।

कथन II: क्रिया और प्रतिक्रिया बलों के बीच कोई कार्य-कारण (कारण और प्रभाव) संबंध निहित नहीं होता है; दोनों में से किसी भी बल को क्रिया और दूसरे को प्रतिक्रिया कहा जा सकता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the First Proposition on the Locus of Third-Law Forces
According to Newton's third law, forces always arise from mutual interactions between pairs of interacting bodies. If body A exerts a force \(\vec{F}_{BA}\) on body B, then body B simultaneously exerts an equal and opposite force \(\vec{F}_{AB} = -\vec{F}_{BA}\) on body A. Because the two forces act on different bodies, they can never act on the same body and cannot cancel each other out on any individual body. Hence, this physical statement is entirely correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Second Proposition on Simultaneity and Symmetry
The terms 'action' and 'reaction' in the third law do not imply a chronological sequence where an action occurs first and produces a reaction subsequently. The two mutual forces occur strictly simultaneously. Any one of the interaction forces can arbitrarily be labelled as the action, and the corresponding opposite partner becomes the reaction. Therefore, this assertion is also scientifically accurate.

Final Conceptual Answer: Both evaluated propositions concerning the mutual, simultaneous, and non-causal nature of third-law forces are scientifically correct.

चरण 1: तीसरे नियम के बलों के कार्य-स्थल का मूल्यांकन
न्यूटन के तीसरे नियम के अनुसार, बल हमेशा दो परस्पर क्रियाशील निकायों के बीच युग्मों में उत्पन्न होते हैं। यदि निकाय A निकाय B पर बल लगाता है, तो B भी A पर समान और विपरीत बल लगाता है। चूंकि दोनों बल दो अलग-अलग निकायों पर लगते हैं, अतः वे कभी एक ही निकाय पर कार्य नहीं करते। यह कथन पूर्णतः सत्य है।

चरण 2: समकालिकता एवं समरूपता का मूल्यांकन
क्रिया और प्रतिक्रिया बलों के मध्य कोई कालानुक्रमिक या कार्य-कारण संबंध नहीं होता है। दोनों बल ठीक एक ही क्षण पर कार्य करते हैं। इनमें से किसी को भी क्रिया और दूसरे को प्रतिक्रिया कहा जा सकता है। अतः यह कथन भी पूर्णतः सत्य है।

अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: तीसरे नियम के बलों की समकालिकता और दो भिन्न निकायों पर कार्य करने से संबंधित दोनों कथन सत्य हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS_11_LAWS_OF_MOTION_STATEMENT_Q03 - Second law as a local law and impulse definition

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Newton's second law is a local relation, meaning that the acceleration of a particle at a given point and instant is determined solely by the net external force acting on it at that specific location and instant.

Statement II: Impulse delivered by a force over an interval of time is equal to the total change in linear momentum produced in that time interval, regardless of whether the force is constant or time-varying.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: न्यूटन का द्वितीय नियम एक स्थानीय (लोकल) संबंध है, जिसका अर्थ है कि किसी दिए गए बिंदु और क्षण पर कण का त्वरण केवल उसी विशिष्ट स्थान और क्षण पर उस पर लगने वाले कुल बाह्य बल द्वारा निर्धारित होता है।

कथन II: किसी समय अंतराल में किसी बल द्वारा दिया गया आवेग उस समय अंतराल में उत्पन्न रैखिक संवेग में कुल परिवर्तन के बराबर होता है, चाहे बल नियत हो या समय के साथ परिवर्ती।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the Local Nature of Newton's Second Law
In Newtonian mechanics, the relation \(\vec{F}(t) = m\vec{a}(t)\) is strictly local in both space and time. The instantaneous acceleration of a particle is governed completely by the net force applied at that precise instant and location; the particle retains no dynamical 'memory' of past forces once those forces cease. For instance, when a stone is dropped from an accelerating vehicle, its horizontal acceleration drops to zero the instant it loses contact with the vehicle (ignoring air drag). This principle is scientifically valid.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Impulse-Momentum Theorem
The impulse \(\vec{J}\) of a force \(\vec{F}\) acting from time \(t_1\) to \(t_2\) is defined by the definite integral:
\[\vec{J} = \int_{t_1}^{t_2} \vec{F}\,dt\]
Substituting \(\vec{F} = \frac{d\vec{p}}{dt}\) into the integral yields:
\[\vec{J} = \int_{t_1}^{t_2} \frac{d\vec{p}}{dt}\,dt = \vec{p}(t_2) - \vec{p}(t_1) = \Delta \vec{p}\]
This fundamental relationship holds unconditionally for constant as well as wildly time-varying forces. Hence, this statement is fully accurate.

Final Conceptual Answer: Both the proposition describing the local character of the second law and the proposition stating the general impulse-momentum theorem are correct.

चरण 1: द्वितीय नियम की स्थानीय प्रकृति का मूल्यांकन
न्यूटन के द्वितीय नियम के अनुसार \(\vec{F}(t) = m\vec{a}(t)\) स्थान और समय दोनों में स्थानीय संबंध है। किसी क्षण कण का त्वरण केवल उसी क्षण लगने वाले बल पर निर्भर करता है, गति के पिछले इतिहास पर नहीं। अतः यह कथन भौतिक रूप से पूर्णतः सही है।

चरण 2: आवेग-संवेग प्रमेय का मूल्यांकन
आवेग की परिभाषा \(\vec{J} = \int_{t_1}^{t_2} \vec{F}\,dt\) होती है। \(\vec{F} = \frac{d\vec{p}}{dt}\) रखने पर \(\vec{J} = \Delta\vec{p}\) प्राप्त होता है, जो नियत अथवा परिवर्ती दोनों प्रकार के बलों के लिए समान रूप से मान्य है। अतः यह कथन भी पूर्णतः सत्य है।

अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: द्वितीय नियम की स्थानीय प्रकृति और आवेग-संवेग संबंध दोनों के प्रतिपादन पूर्णतः सत्य हैं।

answer.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS_11_LAWS_OF_MOTION_STATEMENT_Q04 - Area dependence and self adjusting nature of friction

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The maximum limiting static friction between two dry solid surfaces is directly proportional to the apparent macroscopic area of contact between them.

Statement II: Static friction is a self-adjusting force that matches the magnitude of the applied tending force parallel to the surface up to the limiting threshold \(\mu_s N\).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: दो शुष्क ठोस सतहों के बीच अधिकतम सीमांत स्थैतिक घर्षण उनके बीच संपर्क के आभासी स्थूल क्षेत्रफल के सीधे समानुपाती होता है।

कथन II: स्थैतिक घर्षण एक स्वतः-समायोज्य बल है जो सीमांत मान \(\mu_s N\) तक सतह के समानांतर प्रयुक्त प्रेरक बल के परिमाण से मेल खाता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the First Proposition on Contact Area
According to the empirical laws of dry friction (Amontons' laws), the limiting static friction \(f_{s,\max} = \mu_s N\) is independent of the apparent macroscopic surface area of contact. Although increasing the apparent area spreads the normal force over a larger geometry, the actual microscopic area of contact at the asperities remains directly proportional to the normal load \(N\). Consequently, the limiting frictional resistance does not scale with macroscopic contact area. Therefore, the first proposition is physically incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Second Proposition on Self-Adjustment
Static friction \(f_s\) does not maintain a constant value; it only arises when an external force attempts to produce relative motion. For any applied tangential force \(F_{\text{applied}}\) below the threshold \(\mu_s N\), static friction automatically equals \(F_{\text{applied}}\) to keep the object in translational equilibrium (\(a = 0\)). It adjusts continuously from zero up to the maximum limiting value \(\mu_s N\). Therefore, this second proposition is physically accurate.

Final Conceptual Answer: The proposition claiming that limiting friction depends on apparent contact area is incorrect, whereas the proposition describing static friction as self-adjusting is correct.

चरण 1: संपर्क क्षेत्रफल पर घर्षण की निर्भरता का मूल्यांकन
शुष्क घर्षण के नियमों के अनुसार, सीमांत स्थैतिक घर्षण \(f_{s,\max} = \mu_s N\) संपर्क के आभासी स्थूल क्षेत्रफल पर निर्भर नहीं करता है। वास्तविक सूक्ष्म संपर्क क्षेत्रफल केवल अभिलंब बल के समानुपाती होता है। अतः संपर्क क्षेत्रफल के समानुपाती होने का पहला दावा असत्य है।

चरण 2: स्थैतिक घर्षण के स्वतः-समायोजन का मूल्यांकन
स्थैतिक घर्षण एक स्वतः-समायोज्य बल है जो विरामावस्था बनाए रखने के लिए प्रयुक्त बल के ठीक बराबर परिमाण में उत्पन्न होता है, जब तक कि प्रयुक्त बल \(\mu_s N\) को पार न कर जाए। अतः यह दूसरा कथन पूर्णतः सत्य है।

अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: संपर्क क्षेत्रफल से संबंधित पहला कथन असत्य है, जबकि स्थैतिक घर्षण के स्वतः-समायोजन से संबंधित दूसरा कथन सत्य है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS_11_LAWS_OF_MOTION_STATEMENT_Q05 - Conservation of momentum and kinetic energy during gun recoil

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: When a bullet is fired from a rifle, the total linear momentum of the (rifle + bullet) system remains conserved because the firing forces are strictly internal to the system.

Statement II: Because momentum is conserved during firing, the kinetic energy acquired by the recoiling rifle is equal to the kinetic energy acquired by the ejected bullet.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: जब किसी राइफल से गोली चलाई जाती है, तो (राइफल + गोली) निकाय का कुल रैखिक संवेग संरक्षित रहता है क्योंकि प्रज्वलन बल निकाय के लिए पूर्णतः आंतरिक होते हैं।

कथन II: चूंकि गोलीबारी के दौरान संवेग संरक्षित रहता है, इसलिए प्रतिक्षिप्त राइफल द्वारा प्राप्त गतिज ऊर्जा उत्सर्जित गोली द्वारा प्राप्त गतिज ऊर्जा के बराबर होती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the First Proposition on Momentum Conservation
For the combined system of rifle of mass \(M\) and bullet of mass \(m\), the explosive combustion of gunpowder generates internal action-reaction force pairs. In the absence of an external horizontal force, the net external force on the system is zero (\(\vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = \vec{0}\)). Therefore, by Newton's second law for a system of particles, the total linear momentum is strictly conserved: \(M \vec{V} + m \vec{v} = \vec{0}\). This statement is fully correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Second Proposition on Kinetic Energy Distribution
From momentum conservation, the magnitudes of momenta are equal: \(p_{\text{rifle}} = p_{\text{bullet}} = p\). The kinetic energy of a body with momentum \(p\) and mass \(m\) is given by:
\[K = \frac{p^2}{2m}\]
Comparing kinetic energies for the rifle and the bullet:
\[\frac{K_{\text{rifle}}}{K_{\text{bullet}}} = \frac{\frac{p^2}{2M}}{\frac{p^2}{2m}} = \frac{m}{M}\]
Since the rifle is far more massive than the bullet (\(M \gg m\)), the rifle acquires only a small fraction of the total kinetic energy, whereas the bullet carries the vast majority of the kinetic energy. Hence, the statement that the kinetic energies are equal is physically false.

Final Conceptual Answer: The proposition confirming conservation of linear momentum is correct, whereas the proposition stating that the rifle and bullet gain equal kinetic energy is incorrect.

चरण 1: रैखिक संवेग संरक्षण का मूल्यांकन
गोली और राइफल के निकाय पर क्षैतिज दिशा में कोई बाह्य बल नहीं होता, क्योंकि गैसों का विस्फोट आंतरिक बल उत्पन्न करता है। अतः कुल रैखिक संवेग संरक्षित रहता है (\(M\vec{V} + m\vec{v} = \vec{0}\))। यह कथन पूर्णतः सत्य है।

चरण 2: गतिज ऊर्जा के वितरण का मूल्यांकन
समान संवेग \(p\) होने पर गतिज ऊर्जा \(K = \frac{p^2}{2m}\) द्रव्यमान के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होती है। चूंकि राइफल का द्रव्यमान गोली से बहुत अधिक होता है (\(M \gg m\)), अतः राइफल की गतिज ऊर्जा गोली की तुलना में अत्यंत कम होती है। इसलिए दोनों की गतिज ऊर्जा समान होने का दावा गलत है।

अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: संवेग संरक्षण से संबंधित पहला कथन सही है, जबकि समान गतिज ऊर्जा होने का दूसरा कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS_11_LAWS_OF_MOTION_STATEMENT_Q06 - Apparent weight in upward and downward accelerating elevator

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The apparent weight of an observer in an elevator accelerating upward with acceleration \(a\) is given by \(m(g - a)\).

Statement II: When an elevator cable snaps and the elevator falls freely under gravity, the reading of a weighing scale inside the elevator is \(mg\).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: ऊपर की ओर \(a\) त्वरण से त्वरित हो रही लिफ्ट में प्रेक्षक का आभासी भार \(m(g - a)\) द्वारा दिया जाता है।

कथन II: जब लिफ्ट की केबल टूट जाती है और लिफ्ट गुरुत्वाकर्षण के अधीन स्वतंत्र रूप से गिरती है, तो लिफ्ट के अंदर वजन मापने वाली तुला का पाठ्यांक \(mg\) होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the First Proposition on Upward Acceleration
Consider an observer of mass \(m\) inside an elevator accelerating upward with acceleration \(a\). Choosing upward as the positive direction, Newton's second law gives:
\[N - mg = ma \implies N = m(g + a)\]
The apparent weight registered by a weighing scale is the normal reaction \(N\). Thus, the apparent weight increases to \(m(g + a)\), not \(m(g - a)\). Hence, the first proposition is physically incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Second Proposition on Free Fall
During free fall, the downward acceleration of the elevator is \(a = g\). The equation of motion along the downward direction yields:
\[mg - N = ma \implies N = m(g - a)\]
Substituting \(a = g\) gives:
\[N = m(g - g) = 0\]
The observer and the weighing scale fall with identical acceleration \(g\), meaning the normal contact force between them vanishes. The scale reading drops to zero (the condition of weightlessness), not \(mg\). Hence, the second proposition is also physically incorrect.

Final Conceptual Answer: Both evaluated propositions regarding the apparent weight of the observer in the accelerated elevator are incorrect.

चरण 1: ऊपर की ओर त्वरित लिफ्ट में आभासी भार का मूल्यांकन
जब लिफ्ट ऊपर की ओर \(a\) त्वरण से त्वरित होती है, तो गति का समीकरण \(N - mg = ma\) होता है, जिससे \(N = m(g + a)\) प्राप्त होता है। अतः आभासी भार बढ़ता है, जबकि कथन में \(m(g - a)\) दिया गया है। इसलिए पहला कथन गलत है।

चरण 2: मुक्त पतन में तुला के पाठ्यांक का मूल्यांकन
स्वतंत्र रूप से नीचे गिरती लिफ्ट में त्वरण \(a = g\) होता है। नीचे की ओर समीकरण \(mg - N = ma\) से \(N = m(g - g) = 0\) प्राप्त होता है। अतः तुला का पाठ्यांक शून्य (भारहीनता) होता है, न कि \(mg\)। इसलिए दूसरा कथन भी गलत है।

अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: त्वरित लिफ्ट में आभासी भार से संबंधित दोनों कथन गलत हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS_11_LAWS_OF_MOTION_STATEMENT_Q07 - Mechanics of circular turning on a banked road

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: On a curved road of radius \(R\) banked at an angle \(\theta\), a vehicle traveling at the optimum speed \(v_0 = \sqrt{R g \tan\theta}\) requires zero friction between its tires and the road surface to execute the turn safely.

Statement II: If a vehicle travels on the banked road at a speed greater than \(v_0\), the static frictional force on the vehicle acts directed up the inclined slope of the road.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: \(\theta\) कोण पर झुकी \(R\) त्रिज्या की घुमावदार सड़क पर, इष्टतम चाल \(v_0 = \sqrt{R g \tan\theta}\) से चलने वाले वाहन को सुरक्षित रूप से मुड़ने के लिए उसके टायरों और सड़क की सतह के बीच शून्य घर्षण की आवश्यकता होती है।

कथन II: यदि कोई वाहन झुकी हुई सड़क पर \(v_0\) से अधिक चाल से चलता है, तो वाहन पर लगने वाला स्थैतिक घर्षण बल सड़क के झुके हुए ढलान पर ऊपर की ओर कार्य करता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the First Proposition on Optimum Speed
On a road banked at angle \(\theta\) without friction, the normal reaction \(N\) provides both the vertical support and the inward centripetal acceleration:
\[N \cos\theta = mg \quad \text{and} \quad N \sin\theta = \frac{m v^2}{R}\]
Dividing these equations gives \(\tan\theta = \frac{v^2}{Rg}\), which yields the optimum speed \(v_0 = \sqrt{Rg\tan\theta}\). At this precise speed, the inward horizontal component of the normal reaction alone supplies the necessary centripetal force, and no frictional force along the incline is required. Hence, the first proposition is physically correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Second Proposition on the Direction of Friction at Higher Speeds
When the vehicle moves at a speed \(v > v_0\), the required centripetal acceleration \(\frac{v^2}{R}\) exceeds what \(N\sin\theta\) alone can provide. The vehicle has an impending tendency to skid outward and up the inclined banked surface. Because static friction always opposes impending relative motion, the static frictional force must act down the incline (inward along the slope) to contribute an additional inward component to the centripetal force. Therefore, stating that friction acts up the slope is incorrect (friction acts up the slope only when \(v < v_0\)).

Final Conceptual Answer: The proposition stating that zero friction is required at optimum speed is correct, whereas the proposition stating that friction acts up the incline at speeds exceeding optimum speed is incorrect.

चरण 1: इष्टतम चाल पर गति का मूल्यांकन
झुकी हुई सड़क पर बिना घर्षण के संतुलन के समीकरण \(N\cos\theta = mg\) तथा \(N\sin\theta = \frac{mv^2}{R}\) होते हैं, जिनसे \(v_0 = \sqrt{Rg\tan\theta}\) प्राप्त होता है। इस गति पर केवल अभिलंब बल का क्षैतिज घटक ही आवश्यक अभिकेंद्री बल प्रदान कर देता है, जिससे टायरों और सड़क के बीच शून्य घर्षण की आवश्यकता होती है। अतः पहला कथन पूर्णतः सत्य है।

चरण 2: इष्टतम चाल से अधिक चाल पर घर्षण की दिशा का मूल्यांकन
जब चाल \(v > v_0\) होती है, तो वाहन की ढलान पर ऊपर की ओर फिसलने की प्रवृत्ति होती है। स्थैतिक घर्षण इस आपेक्षिक गति की प्रवृत्ति का विरोध करता है, इसलिए घर्षण बल ढलान के नीचे की ओर (भीतर की ओर) कार्य करता है। ढलान के ऊपर की ओर कार्य करने का दावा गलत है।

अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: इष्टतम चाल पर शून्य घर्षण होने का पहला कथन सही है, जबकि अधिक चाल पर घर्षण के ऊपर की ओर लगने का दूसरा कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS_11_LAWS_OF_MOTION_STATEMENT_Q08 - Dynamics of Atwood machine and string tension

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In an ideal Atwood machine with two unequal masses \(m_1\) and \(m_2\) (where \(m_2 > m_1\)) connected by a massless inextensible string over a frictionless pulley, the tension in the string is equal to the arithmetic mean of their weights, \(\frac{(m_1 + m_2)g}{2}\).

Statement II: The magnitude of the common linear acceleration of both masses in the ideal Atwood machine is given by \(\frac{(m_2 - m_1)g}{m_1 + m_2}\).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एक आदर्श एटवुड मशीन में, जिसमें दो असमान द्रव्यमान \(m_1\) और \(m_2\) (जहाँ \(m_2 > m_1\)) एक घर्षण रहित घिरनी के ऊपर से गुजरने वाली द्रव्यमान रहित अवितान्य डोरी से जुड़े हैं, डोरी में तनाव उनके भारों के समांतर माध्य \(\frac{(m_1 + m_2)g}{2}\) के बराबर होता है।

कथन II: आदर्श एटवुड मशीन में दोनों द्रव्यमानों के उभयनिष्ठ रैखिक त्वरण का परिमाण \(\frac{(m_2 - m_1)g}{m_1 + m_2}\) द्वारा दिया जाता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Derivation and Evaluation of String Tension
Consider the free-body equations of motion for the two hanging masses with common acceleration \(a\):
For mass \(m_1\) accelerating upward: \(T - m_1 g = m_1 a\)
For mass \(m_2\) accelerating downward: \(m_2 g - T = m_2 a\)
Eliminating \(a\) by multiplying the first equation by \(m_2\) and the second by \(m_1\), then adding them gives:
\[m_2 T - m_1 m_2 g + m_1 m_2 g - m_1 T = 2 m_1 m_2 a \implies T = \frac{2 m_1 m_2}{m_1 + m_2} g\]
This exact expression is the harmonic mean of \(m_1 g\) and \(m_2 g\), not their arithmetic mean \(\frac{(m_1 + m_2)g}{2}\). For unequal masses, the harmonic mean is strictly less than the arithmetic mean. Hence, the first proposition is mathematically and physically incorrect.

Step 2: Derivation and Evaluation of Common Acceleration
Subtracting the equation for \(m_1\) from the equation for \(m_2\) gives:
\[(m_2 g - T) + (T - m_1 g) = m_2 a + m_1 a\]
\[(m_2 - m_1)g = (m_1 + m_2)a \implies a = \frac{m_2 - m_1}{m_1 + m_2} g\]
This result matches the second proposition exactly. Hence, the second proposition is physically accurate.

Final Conceptual Answer: The proposition stating that tension equals the arithmetic mean of the weights is incorrect, whereas the proposition for the system acceleration is correct.

चरण 1: डोरी में तनाव का मूल्यांकन
गति के समीकरण \(T - m_1 g = m_1 a\) तथा \(m_2 g - T = m_2 a\) को हल करने पर डोरी में तनाव \(T = \frac{2 m_1 m_2}{m_1 + m_2} g\) प्राप्त होता है। यह मान भारों का हरात्मक माध्य है, न कि समांतर माध्य \(\frac{(m_1 + m_2)g}{2}\)। अतः पहला कथन असत्य है।

चरण 2: निकाय के त्वरण का मूल्यांकन
दोनों समीकरणों को जोड़ने पर: \((m_2 - m_1)g = (m_1 + m_2)a \implies a = \frac{m_2 - m_1}{m_1 + m_2} g\) प्राप्त होता है। यह सूत्र पूर्णतः सही है। अतः दूसरा कथन सत्य है।

अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: डोरी के तनाव से संबंधित पहला कथन असत्य है, जबकि त्वरण से संबंधित दूसरा कथन सत्य है।

answer.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS_11_LAWS_OF_MOTION_STATEMENT_Q01 - Fundamental concepts of Newton first and third laws

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements:

Statement I: Newton's first law of motion asserts that if the net external force acting on a body is zero, its acceleration is identically zero.

Statement II: Newton's third law states that action and reaction forces act simultaneously on two different interacting bodies rather than on the same body.

Statement III: When a projectile thrown vertically upward reaches its highest point where its velocity is momentarily zero, the net force acting on it is zero.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

निम्नलिखित तीन कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: न्यूटन के गति के प्रथम नियम के अनुसार यदि किसी वस्तु पर लगने वाला कुल बाह्य बल शून्य है, तो उसका त्वरण निश्चित रूप से शून्य होता है।

कथन II: न्यूटन का तीसरा नियम बताता है कि क्रिया और प्रतिक्रिया बल एक ही वस्तु के बजाय दो अलग-अलग परस्पर क्रिया करने वाली वस्तुओं पर एक साथ कार्य करते हैं।

कथन III: जब ऊर्ध्वाधर ऊपर की ओर फेंका गया कोई प्रक्षेप्य अपने उच्चतम बिंदु पर पहुंचता है जहाँ उसका वेग क्षण भर के लिए शून्य होता है, तो उस पर कार्य करने वाला कुल बल शून्य होता है।

नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the First Proposition on the First Law of Motion
Newton's first law of motion directly equates translational equilibrium with zero acceleration: if \(\sum \vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = \vec{0}\), then \(\vec{a} = \vec{0}\). A body at rest remains at rest, and a body moving with constant velocity maintains its velocity in a straight line. Thus, the first proposition is physically accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Second Proposition on Third Law Action-Reaction Pairs
According to Newton's third law, forces always occur in mutual interaction pairs. When body A exerts a force on body B, body B simultaneously exerts an equal and opposite force on body A (\(\vec{F}_{AB} = -\vec{F}_{BA}\)). Because the two forces act on different bodies, they can never act on the same body and cannot cancel each other on an individual body. Thus, the second proposition is physically accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Third Proposition on a Momentarily Stationary Projectile
At the highest point of a vertically projected body, its instantaneous velocity \(v = 0\), but the gravitational force exerted by the Earth continues to act downward with magnitude \(F_g = mg\). By Newton's second law, its downward acceleration remains \(a = g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\). Hence, the net force is not zero, making the third proposition physically incorrect.

Final Conceptual Answer: The propositions regarding the first law and the simultaneous action-reaction on distinct bodies are correct, whereas the proposition stating that the net force vanishes at the top of the trajectory is incorrect.

चरण 1: प्रथम नियम संबंधी पहले कथन का मूल्यांकन
न्यूटन के प्रथम नियम के अनुसार, यदि किसी निकाय पर कुल बाह्य बल शून्य है (\(\sum \vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = \vec{0}\)), तो उसका त्वरण शून्य होता है (\(\vec{a} = \vec{0}\))। अतः पहला कथन पूर्णतः सत्य है।

चरण 2: तीसरे नियम संबंधी दूसरे कथन का मूल्यांकन
न्यूटन के तीसरे नियम के अनुसार क्रिया और प्रतिक्रिया बल परस्पर अन्योन्यक्रिया करने वाले दो अलग-अलग निकायों पर एक साथ कार्य करते हैं। अतः दूसरा कथन पूर्णतः सत्य है।

चरण 3: उच्चतम बिंदु पर प्रक्षेप्य संबंधी तीसरे कथन का मूल्यांकन
ऊर्ध्वाधर गति के उच्चतम बिंदु पर क्षणिक वेग \(v = 0\) अवश्य होता है, परंतु पृथ्वी का गुरुत्वाकर्षण बल \(mg\) नीचे की ओर निरंतर कार्य करता रहता है, जिससे त्वरण \(g\) बना रहता है। अतः नेट बल शून्य होने का दावा गलत है।

अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: प्रथम और द्वितीय नियमों से संबंधित पहले दो कथन सही हैं, जबकि उच्चतम बिंदु पर बल शून्य होने संबंधी तीसरा कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Statement I and Statement II only are correct
Statement II and Statement III only are correct
Statement I and Statement III only are correct
Statement I, Statement II, and Statement III are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS_11_LAWS_OF_MOTION_STATEMENT_Q02 - Properties and laws of static and kinetic friction

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements:

Statement I: The limiting value of static friction between two dry surfaces is directly proportional to the apparent macroscopic area of contact.

Statement II: Static friction is a self-adjusting force whose magnitude matches the applied tending force parallel to the interface up to its maximum threshold \(\mu_s N\).

Statement III: The coefficient of kinetic friction \(\mu_k\) between two given solid materials is typically less than the coefficient of static friction \(\mu_s\).

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

निम्नलिखित तीन कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: दो शुष्क सतहों के बीच स्थैतिक घर्षण का सीमांत मान संपर्क के आभासी स्थूल क्षेत्रफल के सीधे समानुपाती होता है।

कथन II: स्थैतिक घर्षण एक स्वतः-समायोज्य बल है जिसका परिमाण संपर्क तल के समानांतर प्रयुक्त प्रेरक बल से मेल खाता है, जब तक कि यह अपनी अधिकतम सीमा \(\mu_s N\) तक न पहुंच जाए।

कथन III: किन्हीं दो दिए गए ठोस पदार्थों के बीच गतिज घर्षण गुणांक \(\mu_k\) आमतौर पर स्थैतिक घर्षण गुणांक \(\mu_s\) से कम होता है।

नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the First Proposition on Contact Area
According to the empirical laws of dry friction, the limiting static friction \(f_{s,\max} = \mu_s N\) is independent of the apparent macroscopic area of contact. Although a larger apparent area spreads the normal force over more surface, the microscopic real contact area at the asperities depends solely on the normal load \(N\). Therefore, claiming that limiting friction is proportional to apparent contact area is incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Second Proposition on Self-Adjustment of Static Friction
Static friction \(f_s\) is not a fixed quantity; it arises only in response to an applied horizontal force attempting to cause relative motion. For any applied force \(F_{\text{applied}} \le \mu_s N\), static friction automatically balances the applied force: \(f_s = F_{\text{applied}}\), ensuring zero acceleration. Thus, this statement is physically accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Third Proposition on Coefficients of Friction
Once relative motion begins, the interlocking asperities between the surfaces do not interlock as deeply as when at rest. Consequently, experimental evidence consistently shows that the kinetic friction coefficient is strictly less than the static friction coefficient (\(\mu_k < \mu_s\)). Therefore, this statement is physically accurate.

Final Conceptual Answer: The propositions regarding the self-adjusting nature of static friction and the inequality between kinetic and static friction coefficients are correct, whereas the proposition claiming dependence on apparent contact area is incorrect.

चरण 1: संपर्क क्षेत्रफल संबंधी पहले कथन का मूल्यांकन
शुष्क घर्षण के नियमों के अनुसार, सीमांत स्थैतिक घर्षण \(f_{s,\max} = \mu_s N\) संपर्क के आभासी स्थूल क्षेत्रफल से स्वतंत्र होता है। अतः संपर्क क्षेत्रफल के समानुपाती होने का पहला दावा गलत है।

चरण 2: स्वतः-समायोजन संबंधी दूसरे कथन का मूल्यांकन
स्थैतिक घर्षण एक स्वतः-समायोज्य बल है जो गति की प्रवृत्ति का विरोध करने के लिए प्रयुक्त बल के ठीक बराबर परिमाण में उत्पन्न होता है (जब तक कि \(F_{\text{applied}} \le \mu_s N\))। अतः दूसरा कथन पूर्णतः सत्य है।

चरण 3: घर्षण गुणांकों के संबंध का मूल्यांकन
सापेक्ष गति प्रारंभ होने पर सूक्ष्म उभारों का अंतर्ग्रथन कमजोर हो जाता है, जिससे गतिज घर्षण गुणांक हमेशा स्थैतिक घर्षण गुणांक से कम होता है (\(\mu_k < \mu_s\))। अतः तीसरा कथन भी पूर्णतः सत्य है।

अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: स्थैतिक घर्षण के स्वतः-समायोजन और गतिज घर्षण गुणांक के स्थैतिक गुणांक से कम होने से संबंधित कथन सही हैं, जबकि संपर्क क्षेत्रफल पर निर्भरता वाला कथन गलत है।

Statement II and Statement III only are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS_11_LAWS_OF_MOTION_STATEMENT_Q03 - Dynamics of level and banked circular roads

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements:

Statement I: On an unbanked level circular road, the centripetal acceleration of a negotiating car is provided solely by the static frictional force between the road and tires.

Statement II: Banking the road surface at an angle \(\theta\) eliminates the normal reaction force exerted by the road on the vehicle tires.

Statement III: At the optimum speed \(v_0 = \sqrt{R g \tan\theta}\) on a banked road, no frictional force is required along the road slope to execute the turn.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

निम्नलिखित तीन कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: बिना ढलान वाली समतल वृत्ताकार सड़क पर, मुड़ने वाली कार का अभिकेंद्री त्वरण पूरी तरह से सड़क और टायरों के बीच स्थैतिक घर्षण बल द्वारा प्रदान किया जाता है।

कथन II: सड़क की सतह को \(\theta\) कोण पर झुकाने (बंकन करने) से सड़क द्वारा वाहन के टायरों पर लगाया जाने वाला अभिलंब प्रतिक्रिया बल समाप्त हो जाता है।

कथन III: झुकी हुई सड़क पर इष्टतम चाल \(v_0 = \sqrt{R g \tan\theta}\) पर मुड़ने के लिए सड़क के ढलान के अनुदिश किसी घर्षण बल की आवश्यकता नहीं होती है।

नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the First Proposition on Level Circular Motion
On a horizontal flat circular path of radius \(R\), the normal reaction acts vertically upward and gravity acts vertically downward. Neither has any horizontal radial component. The only horizontal force available to supply the inward centripetal acceleration \(a_c = \frac{v^2}{R}\) is static friction: \(f_s = \frac{mv^2}{R} \le \mu_s mg\). Thus, the first proposition is physically accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Second Proposition on Normal Reaction on a Banked Road
When a road is banked at an angle \(\theta\), the normal reaction \(N\) tilts toward the center of curvature. Its vertical component balances gravity (\(N\cos\theta = mg + f\sin\theta\)) and its horizontal component \(N\sin\theta\) assists in providing centripetal force. The normal reaction is not eliminated; in fact, its magnitude is non-zero and critical. Thus, the second proposition is physically false.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Third Proposition on Optimum Speed
At the design optimum speed \(v_0\), the horizontal component of the normal reaction alone balances the required centripetal acceleration: \(N\sin\theta = \frac{mv_0^2}{R}\) and \(N\cos\theta = mg\). Dividing these gives \(\tan\theta = \frac{v_0^2}{Rg} \implies v_0 = \sqrt{Rg\tan\theta}\). Under this condition, zero lateral friction is mobilized along the banked slope, eliminating tire wear. Thus, the third proposition is physically accurate.

Final Conceptual Answer: The propositions regarding static friction on flat roads and zero friction at the optimum speed on banked roads are correct, whereas the proposition stating that normal reaction vanishes on banked roads is incorrect.

चरण 1: समतल वृत्ताकार मोड़ संबंधी पहले कथन का मूल्यांकन
समतल सड़क पर ऊर्ध्वाधर बल (भार और अभिलंब प्रतिक्रिया) एक-दूसरे को संतुलित करते हैं। केंद्र की ओर आवश्यक अभिकेंद्री त्वरण केवल स्थैतिक घर्षण बल द्वारा प्रदान किया जाता है (\(f_s = \frac{mv^2}{R}\))। अतः पहला कथन पूर्णतः सत्य है।

चरण 2: झुकी सड़क पर अभिलंब प्रतिक्रिया संबंधी दूसरे कथन का मूल्यांकन
सड़क को झुकाने पर अभिलंब प्रतिक्रिया समाप्त नहीं होती, बल्कि उसका क्षैतिज घटक \(N\sin\theta\) अभिकेंद्री बल प्रदान करने में सहायता करता है। अतः दूसरा कथन गलत है।

चरण 3: इष्टतम चाल संबंधी तीसरे कथन का मूल्यांकन
इष्टतम चाल \(v_0 = \sqrt{Rg\tan\theta}\) पर अभिलंब बल का क्षैतिज घटक ही आवश्यक अभिकेंद्री बल प्रदान कर देता है, जिससे ढलान के अनुदिश किसी घर्षण बल की आवश्यकता नहीं होती। अतः तीसरा कथन पूर्णतः सत्य है।

अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: समतल सड़क पर घर्षण की भूमिका और झुकी सड़क पर इष्टतम चाल से संबंधित कथन सही हैं, जबकि अभिलंब प्रतिक्रिया समाप्त होने संबंधी कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Statement I and Statement II only are correct
Statement II and Statement III only are correct
Statement I and Statement III only are correct
Statement I, Statement II, and Statement III are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS_11_LAWS_OF_MOTION_STATEMENT_Q04 - Momentum conservation Atwood dynamics and elevator free fall

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements:

Statement I: In an isolated system experiencing zero net external force, total linear momentum is conserved in both elastic and completely inelastic collisions.

Statement II: In an ideal Atwood machine with unequal masses \(m_1\) and \(m_2\) (where \(m_2 > m_1\)) over a massless frictionless pulley, the acceleration of the system is \(a = \frac{m_2 - m_1}{m_1 + m_2}g\).

Statement III: An object inside a freely falling elevator experiences apparent weightlessness because the normal contact force exerted by the supporting elevator floor vanishes.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

निम्नलिखित तीन कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: शून्य कुल बाह्य बल का अनुभव करने वाले किसी विलगित निकाय में, कुल रैखिक संवेग प्रत्यास्थ और पूर्णतः अप्रत्यास्थ दोनों प्रकार की टक्करों में संरक्षित रहता है।

कथन II: एक द्रव्यमान रहित घर्षण रहित घिरनी पर दो असमान द्रव्यमानों \(m_1\) और \(m_2\) (जहाँ \(m_2 > m_1\)) वाली आदर्श एटवुड मशीन में निकाय का त्वरण \(a = \frac{m_2 - m_1}{m_1 + m_2}g\) होता है।

कथन III: स्वतंत्र रूप से नीचे गिरती लिफ्ट के अंदर कोई वस्तु आभासी भारहीनता का अनुभव करती है क्योंकि लिफ्ट के फर्श द्वारा लगाया गया अभिलंब संपर्क बल शून्य हो जाता है।

नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the First Proposition on Momentum Conservation
Linear momentum conservation follows directly from Newton's second and third laws applied to an isolated system: \(\frac{d\vec{P}}{dt} = \vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = \vec{0}\). Because collision forces are internal mutual interaction pairs, total linear momentum remains conserved regardless of whether mechanical kinetic energy is conserved (elastic) or converted into heat/sound/deformation (completely inelastic). Thus, the first proposition is physically accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Second Proposition on Atwood Machine Dynamics
For two masses \(m_1\) and \(m_2\) (with \(m_2 > m_1\)) connected by a taut massless string over a frictionless pulley:
For \(m_1\): \(T - m_1 g = m_1 a\)
For \(m_2\): \(m_2 g - T = m_2 a\)
Adding the equations yields \((m_2 - m_1)g = (m_1 + m_2)a \implies a = \frac{m_2 - m_1}{m_1 + m_2}g\). Thus, the second proposition is physically accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Third Proposition on Apparent Weightlessness
Apparent weight is physically defined as the normal reaction \(N\) registered by a scale or floor supporting an object of mass \(m\). In an elevator accelerating downward at \(a\), the equation of motion is \(mg - N = ma \implies N = m(g - a)\). In free fall under gravity, \(a = g\), which gives \(N = m(g - g) = 0\). The vanishing of the normal reaction corresponds to true apparent weightlessness. Thus, the third proposition is physically accurate.

Final Conceptual Answer: All three evaluated propositions concerning momentum conservation, Atwood machine acceleration, and apparent weightlessness in free fall are scientifically correct.

चरण 1: संवेग संरक्षण संबंधी पहले कथन का मूल्यांकन
विलगित निकाय पर बाह्य बल शून्य होने पर आंतरिक बलों के कारण कुल रैखिक संवेग हमेशा संरक्षित रहता है, चाहे संघट्ट (टक्कर) प्रत्यास्थ हो या पूर्णतः अप्रत्यास्थ। अतः पहला कथन पूर्णतः सत्य है।

चरण 2: एटवुड मशीन संबंधी दूसरे कथन का मूल्यांकन
गति के समीकरणों \(T - m_1 g = m_1 a\) तथा \(m_2 g - T = m_2 a\) को जोड़ने पर त्वरण \(a = \frac{m_2 - m_1}{m_1 + m_2}g\) प्राप्त होता है। अतः दूसरा कथन पूर्णतः सत्य है।

चरण 3: भारहीनता संबंधी तीसरे कथन का मूल्यांकन
स्वतंत्र रूप से गिरती लिफ्ट में त्वरण \(a = g\) होने के कारण अभिलंब प्रतिक्रिया बल \(N = m(g - g) = 0\) हो जाता है, जिससे आभासी भारहीनता की स्थिति उत्पन्न होती है। अतः तीसरा कथन भी पूर्णतः सत्य है।

अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: संवेग संरक्षण, एटवुड मशीन के त्वरण और मुक्त पतन में भारहीनता से संबंधित तीनों कथन वैज्ञानिक रूप से सत्य हैं।

Statement II and Statement III only are correct
Statement I and Statement III only are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWS_OF_MOTION_MATCH_LIST_Q01 - Fundamental physical quantities in classical mechanics

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding basic physical concepts in mechanics:

List I (Concept / Quantity) List II (Description / Definition)
A. Inertia I. Product of mass and velocity of a body
B. Linear momentum II. Inherent property resisting any change in the state of rest or uniform motion
C. Impulse of a force III. Product of average force and time duration, equal to change in momentum
D. Centripetal acceleration IV. Inward radial acceleration experienced during uniform circular motion, given by \( \frac{v^2}{R} \)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual definitions of the quantities
The fundamental physical quantities in Newtonian mechanics are defined as follows:

  • Inertia is the inherent property of an object by virtue of which it resists any attempt to change its state of rest or of uniform motion along a straight line. Therefore, inertia corresponds to the inherent property resisting any change in the state of rest or uniform motion.
  • Linear momentum of a body is defined as the product of its mass and velocity, mathematically represented as \( p = mv \).
  • Impulse measures the overall effect of a force acting over a time interval. By the impulse-momentum theorem, impulse equals the product of average force and time interval, which is identical to the resulting change in linear momentum, \( J = F_{\text{avg}} \Delta t = \Delta p \).
  • Centripetal acceleration is the inward radial acceleration required to keep a body moving along a curved circular path of radius \( R \) at speed \( v \), given by \( a_c = \frac{v^2}{R} \).

Step 2: Matching each pair
Pairing each item according to its physical definition:

  • Inertia matches with the inherent property resisting any change in the state of rest or uniform motion (A-II).
  • Linear momentum matches with the product of mass and velocity of a body (B-I).
  • Impulse of a force matches with the product of average force and time duration, equal to change in momentum (C-III).
  • Centripetal acceleration matches with the inward radial acceleration experienced during uniform circular motion (D-IV).

Step 3: Final Answer
The correct combination is A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWS_OF_MOTION_MATCH_LIST_Q02 - Characteristics and properties of various frictions

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the characteristics of different types of friction:

List I (Type of Friction) List II (Characteristic Feature)
A. Static friction I. Maximum threshold value given by \( \mu_s N \) beyond which sliding starts
B. Limiting friction II. Resistance arising due to momentary deformation of surfaces in contact when an object rolls
C. Kinetic friction III. Opposes actual relative sliding between contact surfaces and is nearly independent of sliding speed
D. Rolling friction IV. Self-adjusting resistive force that opposes impending motion and satisfies \( 0 \le f_s \le f_{s,\max} \)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual principles of friction
The laws and features governing frictional forces in mechanics are:

  • Static friction is a self-adjusting contact force that comes into play when there is an applied force attempting to cause relative motion. It opposes impending relative motion and increases from zero up to a maximum threshold value, satisfying \( 0 \le f_s \le f_{s,\max} \).
  • Limiting friction is the maximum possible static frictional force that surfaces can exert before sliding begins, given by \( f_{s,\max} = \mu_s N \).
  • Kinetic friction comes into play when there is actual relative sliding motion between two contact surfaces. It opposes the relative motion and remains nearly independent of the relative sliding velocity over a wide range of speeds.
  • Rolling friction arises when a spherical or cylindrical body rolls over a surface. Because of contact pressure, momentary deformation of the surfaces occurs, causing a small resistance to rolling motion that is much smaller than kinetic friction.

Step 2: Matching each pair
Connecting each type of friction to its characteristic property:

  • Static friction matches with the self-adjusting resistive force that opposes impending motion and satisfies \( 0 \le f_s \le f_{s,\max} \) (A-IV).
  • Limiting friction matches with the maximum threshold value given by \( \mu_s N \) beyond which sliding starts (B-I).
  • Kinetic friction matches with opposing actual relative sliding and being nearly independent of sliding speed (C-III).
  • Rolling friction matches with the resistance arising due to momentary deformation of surfaces in contact when an object rolls (D-II).

Step 3: Final Answer
The correct combination is A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWS_OF_MOTION_MATCH_LIST_Q03 - Governing equations for various mechanical systems

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the dynamics of circular motion on roads:

List I (Physical Situation) List II (Mathematical Expression)
A. Maximum safe speed on an unbanked level circular road of radius \( R \) I. \( \sqrt{\frac{R g (\mu_s + \tan\theta)}{1 - \mu_s \tan\theta}} \)
B. Optimum speed on a banked circular road where no frictional force is needed II. \( \sqrt{\mu_s R g} \)
C. Maximum permissible speed on a banked circular road with friction coefficient \( \mu_s \) III. \( \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{v^2}{R g}\right) \)
D. Banking angle \( \theta \) designed for a vehicle travelling at speed \( v \) IV. \( \sqrt{R g \tan\theta} \)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Derivations for circular motion on roads
Let us examine the force balance for each case:

  • On an unbanked horizontal circular road of radius \( R \), the centripetal force is provided entirely by static friction: \( f_s = \frac{m v^2}{R} \). Since \( f_s \le \mu_s N = \mu_s mg \), the maximum safe speed is \( v_{\max} = \sqrt{\mu_s R g} \).
  • On a banked road of inclination \( \theta \), the horizontal component of normal reaction \( N \sin\theta \) provides centripetal acceleration, while \( N \cos\theta = mg \). When no lateral frictional force is called upon, the speed is optimum: \( \frac{N \sin\theta}{N \cos\theta} = \tan\theta = \frac{v_0^2}{R g} \implies v_0 = \sqrt{R g \tan\theta} \).
  • When a vehicle moves at the maximum possible speed on a banked road, friction acts downward along the slope. Balancing horizontal and vertical forces gives \( N \sin\theta + f_s \cos\theta = \frac{m v_{\max}^2}{R} \) and \( N \cos\theta - f_s \sin\theta = mg \). Substituting \( f_s = \mu_s N \) yields \( v_{\max} = \sqrt{\frac{R g (\mu_s + \tan\theta)}{1 - \mu_s \tan\theta}} \).
  • To design a road so that vehicles rounding a curve of radius \( R \) at speed \( v \) experience zero wear and tear from friction, the banking angle must satisfy \( \tan\theta = \frac{v^2}{R g} \implies \theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{v^2}{R g}\right) \).

Step 2: Matching each situation with its expression
Connecting each circular motion scenario to its formula:

  • Maximum safe speed on an unbanked level circular road matches with \( \sqrt{\mu_s R g} \) (A-II).
  • Optimum speed on a banked circular road with zero friction matches with \( \sqrt{R g \tan\theta} \) (B-IV).
  • Maximum permissible speed on a banked circular road with friction matches with \( \sqrt{\frac{R g (\mu_s + \tan\theta)}{1 - \mu_s \tan\theta}} \) (C-I).
  • Banking angle designed for a speed \( v \) matches with \( \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{v^2}{R g}\right) \) (D-III).

Step 3: Final Answer
The correct combination is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWS_OF_MOTION_MATCH_LIST_Q04 - Apparent weight in different accelerated frames

questiontext.text:
A person of mass \( m \) stands on a weighing scale placed on the floor of an elevator. Match List-I with List-II regarding the apparent weight \( R \) recorded by the scale in various states of motion:

List I (Motion of Elevator) List II (Reading of Weighing Scale \( R \))
A. Accelerating upwards with a constant acceleration \( a \) I. \( R = m(g - a) \)
B. Accelerating downwards with a constant acceleration \( a \) (where \( a < g \)) II. \( R = 0 \) (State of weightlessness)
C. Elevator cable breaks and it falls freely under gravity (\( a = g \)) III. \( R = m(g + a) \)
D. Moving upwards or downwards with a constant velocity \( v \) IV. \( R = mg \) (True gravitational weight)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Free-body diagram and equations of motion
Let \( R \) be the normal reaction force exerted by the scale on the person, and \( mg \) be the downward gravitational force. The reading of the scale equals \( R \).

  • When the elevator accelerates upwards with acceleration \( a \), the net upward force is \( R - mg = ma \). Solving for the apparent weight gives \( R = m(g + a) \).
  • When the elevator accelerates downwards with acceleration \( a < g \), the net downward force is \( mg - R = ma \). Solving for the apparent weight gives \( R = m(g - a) \).
  • When the lift falls freely under gravity, the downward acceleration is \( a = g \). The equation of motion becomes \( mg - R = mg \implies R = m(g - g) = 0 \), corresponding to the condition of weightlessness.
  • When the elevator moves with constant velocity (either upwards or downwards), the net acceleration is zero (\( a = 0 \)). The equation of motion gives \( R - mg = 0 \implies R = mg \), which equals the person's true gravitational weight.

Step 2: Matching each motion to the resulting apparent weight
Matching each case:

  • Accelerating upwards with acceleration \( a \) matches with \( R = m(g + a) \) (A-III).
  • Accelerating downwards with acceleration \( a < g \) matches with \( R = m(g - a) \) (B-I).
  • Falling freely under gravity matches with \( R = 0 \), the state of weightlessness (C-II).
  • Moving with constant velocity matches with \( R = mg \), the true gravitational weight (D-IV).

Step 3: Final Answer
The correct combination is A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWSOFMOTION_NUMERICAL_Q01 - Net force on vertically projected pebble at apex

questiontext.text: A pebble of mass \(0.05\text{ kg}\) is thrown vertically upwards with an initial speed. Neglecting air resistance and taking \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\), what is the magnitude and direction of the net force acting on the pebble at the highest point where it is momentarily at rest?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of pebble: \(m = 0.05\text{ kg}\). Acceleration due to gravity: \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\). Velocity at the apex: \(v = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}\). Air resistance is negligible.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Choose vertically downward direction as positive for the gravitational force. Gravitational field is uniform near Earth's surface.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
According to Newton's second law, \(F_{\text{net}} = m a\). For an object in free flight under gravity alone, the only force acting on it at all points (including the highest point) is the force of gravity: \(W = m g\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given values into the gravitational force equation: \(F_{\text{net}} = 0.05\text{ kg} \times 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2} = 0.49\text{ N}\). Since gravity acts towards the centre of the Earth, the direction of this force is vertically downwards.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Check units: \(\text{kg} \times \text{m s}^{-2} = \text{N}\). The magnitude is \(0.49\text{ N}\) directed vertically downwards, despite instantaneous velocity being zero.

Final Conceptual Answer: \(0.49\text{ N}\), vertically downwards

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWSOFMOTION_NUMERICAL_Q02 - Net force acting on falling terminal raindrop

questiontext.text: A raindrop of mass \(0.04\text{ g}\) is falling vertically downwards with a constant terminal velocity of \(9\text{ m s}^{-1}\). What is the magnitude of the net force acting on the raindrop?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of raindrop: \(m = 0.04\text{ g} = 4 \times 10^{-5}\text{ kg}\). Speed: \(v = 9\text{ m s}^{-1}\) (constant terminal velocity).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Motion is along the vertical direction. Constant velocity implies zero acceleration.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Newton's first and second laws state that if an object moves with constant velocity (\(\vec{v} = \text{constant}\)), its acceleration is \(\vec{a} = \frac{\mathrm{d}\vec{v}}{\mathrm{d}t} = 0\). The net force is \(\vec{F}_{\text{net}} = m \vec{a}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Since the velocity is constant, \(\vec{a} = 0\). Therefore: \(F_{\text{net}} = m \times 0 = 0\text{ N}\). (The upward viscous drag exactly balances the downward gravitational pull).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Terminal velocity denotes dynamic equilibrium where net external force is identically zero. Thus, the net force is \(0\text{ N}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(0\text{ N}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWSOFMOTION_NUMERICAL_Q03 - Horizontal force on stone on train floor

questiontext.text: A stone of mass \(0.1\text{ kg}\) lies at rest on the floor of a train that is accelerating horizontally at \(1.0\text{ m s}^{-2}\). The stone remains stationary relative to the train. What is the net horizontal force acting on the stone?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of stone: \(m = 0.1\text{ kg}\). Horizontal acceleration of the train: \(a = 1.0\text{ m s}^{-2}\). The stone is at rest relative to the train.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Observe the stone from an inertial ground reference frame. The stone shares the horizontal acceleration of the train.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
From Newton's second law in an inertial frame, the net horizontal force providing acceleration \(a\) is \(F_{\text{net}} = m a\). Here, this net horizontal force is provided by static friction between the floor and the stone.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values: \(F_{\text{net}} = 0.1\text{ kg} \times 1.0\text{ m s}^{-2} = 0.1\text{ N}\). The force acts in the direction of motion of the train.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Check units: \(\text{kg} \times \text{m s}^{-2} = \text{N}\). The magnitude is \(0.1\text{ N}\) in the forward horizontal direction.

Final Conceptual Answer: \(0.1\text{ N}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWSOFMOTION_NUMERICAL_Q04 - Stopping time for body under retarding force

questiontext.text: A constant retarding force of \(50\text{ N}\) is applied to a body of mass \(20\text{ kg}\) moving initially with a speed of \(15\text{ m s}^{-1}\). How long does the body take to stop?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of body: \(m = 20\text{ kg}\). Initial velocity: \(u = 15\text{ m s}^{-1}\). Final velocity: \(v = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}\). Retarding force: \(F = -50\text{ N}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Direction of initial motion is positive. Retarding force opposes motion and is therefore negative.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Acceleration: \(a = \frac{F}{m}\). Kinematic relation: \(v = u + a t \implies t = \frac{v - u}{a}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate acceleration: \(a = \frac{-50\text{ N}}{20\text{ kg}} = -2.5\text{ m s}^{-2}\). Calculate stopping time: \(t = \frac{0 - 15\text{ m s}^{-1}}{-2.5\text{ m s}^{-2}} = 6.0\text{ s}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Check units: \(\frac{\text{m s}^{-1}}{\text{m s}^{-2}} = \text{s}\). The time required to stop is \(6.0\text{ s}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(6.0\text{ s}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWSOFMOTION_NUMERICAL_Q05 - Constant force altering speed of moving body

questiontext.text: A constant force acting on a body of mass \(3.0\text{ kg}\) changes its speed from \(2.0\text{ m s}^{-1}\) to \(3.5\text{ m s}^{-1}\) in \(25\text{ s}\). The direction of motion of the body remains unchanged. What is the magnitude of the force?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass: \(m = 3.0\text{ kg}\). Initial speed: \(u = 2.0\text{ m s}^{-1}\). Final speed: \(v = 3.5\text{ m s}^{-1}\). Time interval: \(t = 25\text{ s}\). Motion is unidirectional.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Forward direction of motion is taken as positive. Acceleration is uniform.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Acceleration: \(a = \frac{v - u}{t}\). Newton's second law: \(F = m a\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate acceleration: \(a = \frac{3.5 - 2.0}{25} = \frac{1.5}{25} = 0.06\text{ m s}^{-2}\). Calculate force: \(F = 3.0\text{ kg} \times 0.06\text{ m s}^{-2} = 0.18\text{ N}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Check units: \(\text{kg} \times \text{m s}^{-2} = \text{N}\). The magnitude of the force is \(0.18\text{ N}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(0.18\text{ N}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWSOFMOTION_NUMERICAL_Q06 - Acceleration of body under two perpendicular forces

questiontext.text: A body of mass \(5.0\text{ kg}\) is acted upon by two perpendicular forces of magnitudes \(8\text{ N}\) and \(6\text{ N}\). What is the magnitude of the acceleration of the body?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of body: \(m = 5.0\text{ kg}\). Force 1: \(F_1 = 8\text{ N}\). Force 2: \(F_2 = 6\text{ N}\). Angle between forces: \(\theta = 90^\circ\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The two forces act concurrently on a point mass in a plane.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Resultant force magnitude: \(F_{\text{net}} = \sqrt{F_1^2 + F_2^2 + 2F_1F_2\cos(90^\circ)} = \sqrt{F_1^2 + F_2^2}\). Acceleration: \(a = \frac{F_{\text{net}}}{m}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate resultant force: \(F_{\text{net}} = \sqrt{8^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{64 + 36} = \sqrt{100} = 10\text{ N}\). Calculate acceleration: \(a = \frac{10\text{ N}}{5.0\text{ kg}} = 2.0\text{ m s}^{-2}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Check units: \(\text{N}/\text{kg} = \text{m s}^{-2}\). The acceleration magnitude is \(2.0\text{ m s}^{-2}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(2.0\text{ m s}^{-2}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWSOFMOTION_NUMERICAL_Q07 - Impulse imparted to cricket ball struck back

questiontext.text: A batsman hits back a cricket ball of mass \(0.15\text{ kg}\) straight in the direction of the bowler without altering its initial speed of \(12\text{ m s}^{-1}\). If the ball moves back along the same straight line, what is the magnitude of the impulse imparted to the ball?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of ball: \(m = 0.15\text{ kg}\). Initial velocity: \(u = +12\text{ m s}^{-1}\). Final velocity: \(v = -12\text{ m s}^{-1}\) (reversed direction along same line).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Take the bowler-to-batsman direction as positive, so batsman-to-bowler is negative.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Impulse equals the change in linear momentum: \(I = \Delta p = p_f - p_i = m(v - u)\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate momentum change: \(I = 0.15 \times [(-12) - (+12)] = 0.15 \times (-24) = -3.6\text{ N s}\). The magnitude of the impulse is \(|I| = 3.6\text{ N s}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Check units: \(\text{kg} \times \text{m s}^{-1} = \text{N s}\). The magnitude of impulse is \(3.6\text{ N s}\) (or \(\text{kg m s}^{-1}\)).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(3.6\text{ N s}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWSOFMOTION_NUMERICAL_Q08 - Horizontal force on stone dropped from accelerating train

questiontext.text: A stone of mass \(0.1\text{ kg}\) is dropped from the window of a train accelerating horizontally with \(1.0\text{ m s}^{-2}\). What is the magnitude of the net horizontal force acting on the stone immediately after it is released (neglecting air resistance)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of stone: \(m = 0.1\text{ kg}\). Train acceleration before release: \(a_{\text{train}} = 1.0\text{ m s}^{-2}\). The stone has just been released and is in free flight.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
In an inertial ground frame, once the stone leaves contact with the train window, no horizontal contact force acts on it. Air resistance is neglected.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
According to Newton's first law, a body in flight without horizontal external forces maintains constant horizontal velocity. The net horizontal force is \(F_{\text{horizontal}} = m a_x\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Since there is no horizontal contact or field force acting on the detached stone, \(F_{\text{horizontal}} = 0\text{ N}\). (The only force acting on it is gravity, which acts purely vertically downwards).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Newton's laws are local in time: immediate force depends only on present interactions, not on past contact. Thus, the horizontal force is \(0\text{ N}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(0\text{ N}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWSOFMOTION_NUMERICAL_Q09 - Average resistive force on stopped bullet in block

questiontext.text: A bullet of mass \(0.04\text{ kg}\) moving with a speed of \(90\text{ m s}^{-1}\) enters a heavy wooden block and is stopped after penetrating a distance of \(60\text{ cm}\). What is the average resistive force exerted by the block on the bullet?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of bullet: \(m = 0.04\text{ kg}\). Initial speed: \(u = 90\text{ m s}^{-1}\). Final speed: \(v = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}\). Penetration distance: \(s = 60\text{ cm} = 0.60\text{ m}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Assume uniform deceleration inside the block. Take direction of bullet motion as positive.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
From kinematics: \(v^2 - u^2 = 2as \implies a = \frac{v^2 - u^2}{2s}\). From Newton's second law: \(F = ma\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate acceleration: \(a = \frac{0 - (90)^2}{2 \times 0.60} = \frac{-8100}{1.2} = -6750\text{ m s}^{-2}\). Calculate resistive force: \(F = 0.04\text{ kg} \times (-6750\text{ m s}^{-2}) = -270\text{ N}\). The magnitude of the average resistive force is \(270\text{ N}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Check work-energy: \(\frac{1}{2} m u^2 = \frac{1}{2}(0.04)(8100) = 162\text{ J}\). Force \(= \frac{W}{s} = \frac{162\text{ J}}{0.60\text{ m}} = 270\text{ N}\). Consistent.

Final Conceptual Answer: \(270\text{ N}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWSOFMOTION_NUMERICAL_Q10 - Net force on particle with quadratic position equation

questiontext.text: The vertical position of a particle of mass \(m\) as a function of time \(t\) is described by \(y(t) = ut + \frac{1}{2}gt^2\), where \(u\) and \(g\) are constants. According to Newton's second law, what is the net force acting on the particle?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of particle: \(m\). Position function: \(y(t) = ut + \frac{1}{2}gt^2\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
One-dimensional motion along the vertical \(y\)-axis.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Velocity: \(v(t) = \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}\). Acceleration: \(a(t) = \frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}t}\). Force: \(F = ma\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
First derivative: \(v(t) = \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left(ut + \frac{1}{2}gt^2\right) = u + gt\). Second derivative: \(a(t) = \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(u + gt) = g\). Force: \(F = m a = m g\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The acceleration is constant and equals \(g\). Thus, the net force acting on the particle is \(mg\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(mg\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWSOFMOTION_NUMERICAL_Q11 - Average retarding force stopping three wheeler for child

questiontext.text: A driver of a three-wheeler moving with a speed of \(36\text{ km h}^{-1}\) sees a child standing in the middle of the road and brings his vehicle to rest in \(4.0\text{ s}\) just in time to save the child. If the mass of the three-wheeler is \(400\text{ kg}\) and the mass of the driver is \(65\text{ kg}\), what is the average retarding force on the vehicle and driver system?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Total mass of system: \(M = 400\text{ kg} + 65\text{ kg} = 465\text{ kg}\). Initial speed: \(u = 36\text{ km h}^{-1} = 36 \times \frac{5}{18}\text{ m s}^{-1} = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}\). Final speed: \(v = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}\). Stopping time: \(t = 4.0\text{ s}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Assume uniform deceleration along a straight horizontal path.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Acceleration: \(a = \frac{v - u}{t}\). Retarding force: \(F_{\text{ret}} = M |a|\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate acceleration: \(a = \frac{0 - 10}{4.0} = -2.5\text{ m s}^{-2}\). Calculate magnitude of force: \(F_{\text{ret}} = 465\text{ kg} \times 2.5\text{ m s}^{-2} = 1162.5\text{ N} \approx 1.16 \times 10^3\text{ N}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Check units: \(\text{kg} \times \text{m s}^{-2} = \text{N}\). The average retarding force is \(1.16 \times 10^3\text{ N}\) (or \(1162.5\text{ N}\)).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(1.16 \times 10^3\text{ N}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWSOFMOTION_NUMERICAL_Q12 - Initial blast off thrust for vertically accelerating rocket

questiontext.text: A rocket with a lift-off mass of \(20{,}000\text{ kg}\) is blasted upwards with an initial acceleration of \(5.0\text{ m s}^{-2}\). Taking \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\), what is the initial upward thrust (force) of the blast?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Lift-off mass of rocket: \(m = 20{,}000\text{ kg} = 2.0 \times 10^4\text{ kg}\). Upward acceleration: \(a = 5.0\text{ m s}^{-2}\). Acceleration due to gravity: \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Choose vertically upward as positive. The upward thrust force \(T\) acts upwards, while gravity \(mg\) acts downwards.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Newton's second law: \(F_{\text{net}} = T - mg = ma \implies T = m(g + a)\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute values: \(T = 20{,}000\text{ kg} \times (9.8 + 5.0)\text{ m s}^{-2} = 20{,}000 \times 14.8 = 296{,}000\text{ N} = 2.96 \times 10^5\text{ N}\) (or \(\approx 3.0 \times 10^5\text{ N}\) if \(g = 10\)).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Check units: \(\text{kg} \times \text{m s}^{-2} = \text{N}\). The required blast thrust is \(2.96 \times 10^5\text{ N}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(2.96 \times 10^5\text{ N}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWSOFMOTION_NUMERICAL_Q13 - Recoil speed of radioactive nucleus upon disintegration

questiontext.text: A nucleus is at rest in the laboratory frame of reference. Show that if it disintegrates into two smaller nuclei, the products must fly off in opposite directions. If the ratio of their masses is \(1 : 2\) and the lighter fragment moves with a speed of \(1.6 \times 10^7\text{ m s}^{-1}\), what is the speed of the heavier fragment?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial total momentum: \(\vec{p}_i = 0\). Mass ratio: \(\frac{m_1}{m_2} = \frac{1}{2}\). Speed of lighter fragment: \(v_1 = 1.6 \times 10^7\text{ m s}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
No external force acts on the disintegrating nucleus, so the principle of conservation of linear momentum holds strictly.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Conservation of linear momentum: \(\vec{p}_1 + \vec{p}_2 = 0 \implies m_1 \vec{v}_1 = -m_2 \vec{v}_2\). Therefore, the fragments move in opposite directions, and their speeds satisfy \(m_1 v_1 = m_2 v_2\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Solve for \(v_2\): \(v_2 = \frac{m_1}{m_2} v_1 = \frac{1}{2} \times (1.6 \times 10^7\text{ m s}^{-1}) = 8.0 \times 10^6\text{ m s}^{-1}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Check ratio: \(\frac{v_1}{v_2} = \frac{1.6 \times 10^7}{0.8 \times 10^7} = 2 = \frac{m_2}{m_1}\). This is physically consistent with momentum conservation. The speed of the heavier fragment is \(8.0 \times 10^6\text{ m s}^{-1}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(8.0 \times 10^6\text{ m s}^{-1}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWSOFMOTION_NUMERICAL_Q14 - Impulse exchanged between identical colliding billiard balls

questiontext.text: Two identical billiard balls each of mass \(0.05\text{ kg}\) moving in opposite directions with speed \(6\text{ m s}^{-1}\) collide head-on and rebound with the same speed. What is the magnitude of the impulse imparted to each ball by the other?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of each ball: \(m = 0.05\text{ kg}\). Speed before collision: \(u = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}\). Speed after collision: \(v = -6\text{ m s}^{-1}\) (rebounding with reversed direction).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Take the initial direction of motion of the ball under consideration as positive.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Impulse imparted to a body equals change in its linear momentum: \(I = \Delta p = m(v - u)\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the change in momentum: \(I = 0.05\text{ kg} \times [(-6) - (+6)]\text{ m s}^{-1} = 0.05 \times (-12) = -0.6\text{ N s}\). The magnitude of the impulse is \(|I| = 0.6\text{ N s}\) (or \(\text{kg m s}^{-1}\)). By Newton's third law, the impulse on the second ball is equal in magnitude and opposite in direction (\(+0.6\text{ N s}\)).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Check units: \(\text{kg} \times \text{m s}^{-1} = \text{N s}\). The magnitude for each ball is \(0.6\text{ N s}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(0.6\text{ N s}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWSOFMOTION_NUMERICAL_Q15 - Recoil speed of gun firing shell horizontally

questiontext.text: A gun of mass \(100\text{ kg}\) fires a shell of mass \(0.02\text{ kg}\) with a muzzle speed of \(80\text{ m s}^{-1}\). What is the recoil speed of the gun?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of gun: \(M = 100\text{ kg}\). Mass of shell: \(m = 0.02\text{ kg}\). Muzzle speed of shell: \(v = 80\text{ m s}^{-1}\). Initial system is at rest.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Take the forward direction of the shell as positive. External horizontal forces are negligible during firing.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
By conservation of linear momentum: \(P_{\text{initial}} = P_{\text{final}} \implies 0 = M V + m v \implies V = -\frac{m v}{M}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute values: \(V = -\frac{0.02\text{ kg} \times 80\text{ m s}^{-1}}{100\text{ kg}} = -\frac{1.6}{100} = -0.016\text{ m s}^{-1} = -1.6\text{ cm s}^{-1}\). The recoil speed (magnitude) is \(0.016\text{ m s}^{-1}\) (or \(1.6\text{ cm s}^{-1}\)).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Check momentum: \(100 \times 0.016 = 1.6\text{ kg m s}^{-1}\), which balances the shell's momentum \(0.02 \times 80 = 1.6\text{ kg m s}^{-1}\). Recoil speed is \(0.016\text{ m s}^{-1}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(0.016\text{ m s}^{-1}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWSOFMOTION_NUMERICAL_Q16 - Maximum acceleration of train keeping resting box stationary

questiontext.text: A box of mass \(40\text{ kg}\) rests on the floor of a train. The coefficient of static friction between the box and the train floor is \(\mu_s = 0.15\). Taking \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\), what is the maximum acceleration of the train in which the box remains stationary relative to the train?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of box: \(m = 40\text{ kg}\). Coefficient of static friction: \(\mu_s = 0.15\). Acceleration due to gravity: \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Horizontal acceleration of the train causes static friction to accelerate the box forward so that no relative slipping occurs.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The maximum available static friction is \(f_{s,\max} = \mu_s N = \mu_s mg\). The required accelerating force is \(F = ma\). For no slipping: \(ma \le \mu_s mg \implies a_{\max} = \mu_s g\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate maximum acceleration: \(a_{\max} = 0.15 \times 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2} = 1.47\text{ m s}^{-2} \approx 1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Check independence of mass: \(m\) cancels out completely. The maximum allowable acceleration is \(1.47\text{ m s}^{-2}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(1.47\text{ m s}^{-2}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWSOFMOTION_NUMERICAL_Q17 - Coefficient of static friction from limiting incline angle

questiontext.text: A mass of \(4\text{ kg}\) rests on a horizontal plane. The plane is gradually inclined until at an angle of \(\theta = 15^\circ\) with the horizontal, the mass just begins to slide. What is the coefficient of static friction between the block and the surface? (Given: \(\tan 15^\circ \approx 0.27\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of block: \(m = 4\text{ kg}\). Angle of repose: \(\theta = 15^\circ\). The block is on the verge of sliding.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Decompose forces parallel and perpendicular to the inclined plane. Equilibrium holds up to the critical angle of repose.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Perpendicular to incline: \(N = mg \cos\theta\). Parallel to incline at verge of motion: \(f_{s,\max} = mg \sin\theta\). Since \(f_{s,\max} = \mu_s N\), we have \(\mu_s = \tan\theta\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the critical angle: \(\mu_s = \tan(15^\circ) = 2 - \sqrt{3} \approx 2 - 1.732 = 0.268 \approx 0.27\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Check dimensions: coefficient of friction is dimensionless. The coefficient of static friction is \(0.27\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(0.27\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWSOFMOTION_NUMERICAL_Q18 - Maximum safe turning speed on level road

questiontext.text: A cyclist speeding at \(18\text{ km h}^{-1}\) on a level road takes a sharp circular turn of radius \(3\text{ m}\) without reducing speed. The coefficient of static friction between the tyres and the road is \(\mu_s = 0.10\). Taking \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\), what is the maximum speed with which the cyclist can negotiate the turn without slipping?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Radius of turn: \(R = 3\text{ m}\). Coefficient of static friction: \(\mu_s = 0.10\). Acceleration due to gravity: \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\). Current speed: \(v = 18\text{ km h}^{-1} = 5.0\text{ m s}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Horizontal unbanked circular curve where static friction provides the inward centripetal acceleration.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Centripetal requirement: \(\frac{m v^2}{R} \le \mu_s N = \mu_s mg \implies v_{\max} = \sqrt{\mu_s R g}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the maximum permissible speed: \(v_{\max} = \sqrt{0.10 \times 3\text{ m} \times 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}} = \sqrt{2.94}\text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 1.71\text{ m s}^{-1}\). (Because \(5.0\text{ m s}^{-1} > 1.71\text{ m s}^{-1}\), the cyclist would slip at \(18\text{ km h}^{-1}\)).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Check units: \(\sqrt{\text{m} \times \text{m s}^{-2}} = \text{m s}^{-1}\). Thus, the maximum speed to avoid slipping is \(1.71\text{ m s}^{-1}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(1.71\text{ m s}^{-1}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWSOFMOTION_NUMERICAL_Q19 - Optimum vehicle speed on frictionless banked racetrack

questiontext.text: A circular racetrack of radius \(300\text{ m}\) is banked at an angle of \(15^\circ\). Taking \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\) and \(\tan 15^\circ \approx 0.268\), what is the optimum speed of a racecar to negotiate the turn without any wear and tear on its tyres (i.e. zero frictional force needed)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Radius of banked curve: \(R = 300\text{ m}\). Banking angle: \(\theta = 15^\circ\). \(\tan 15^\circ = 0.268\). Acceleration due to gravity: \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Wear and tear is minimized when no frictional force is required, so the horizontal component of the normal reaction provides the entire centripetal acceleration.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
From the equilibrium of normal force components: \(N \cos\theta = mg\) and \(N \sin\theta = \frac{m v_0^2}{R}\). Dividing gives the optimum speed: \(v_0 = \sqrt{R g \tan\theta}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate \(v_0\): \(v_0 = \sqrt{300\text{ m} \times 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2} \times 0.268} = \sqrt{2940 \times 0.268} = \sqrt{787.92} \approx 28.1\text{ m s}^{-1}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Convert to \(\text{km h}^{-1}\): \(28.1 \times 3.6 \approx 101\text{ km h}^{-1}\). The optimum speed is \(28.1\text{ m s}^{-1}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(28.1\text{ m s}^{-1}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWSOFMOTION_NUMERICAL_Q20 - Maximum permissible speed on banked circular racetrack

questiontext.text: A circular racetrack of radius \(300\text{ m}\) is banked at an angle of \(15^\circ\). The coefficient of static friction between the wheels and the road is \(\mu_s = 0.20\). Taking \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\) and \(\tan 15^\circ \approx 0.268\), what is the maximum permissible speed of the car to avoid slipping outwards?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Radius: \(R = 300\text{ m}\). Banking angle: \(\theta = 15^\circ\) (\(\tan 15^\circ \approx 0.268\)). Coefficient of static friction: \(\mu_s = 0.20\). \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
At maximum speed, static friction acts down the incline to prevent outward slipping.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The maximum permissible speed on a banked road with friction is given by: \(v_{\max} = \sqrt{R g \left(\frac{\mu_s + \tan\theta}{1 - \mu_s \tan\theta}\right)}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the numerator and denominator of the factor: \(\mu_s + \tan\theta = 0.20 + 0.268 = 0.468\). \(1 - \mu_s \tan\theta = 1 - (0.20 \times 0.268) = 1 - 0.0536 = 0.9464\). Ratio: \(\frac{0.468}{0.9464} \approx 0.4945\). Now compute \(v_{\max}\): \(v_{\max} = \sqrt{300 \times 9.8 \times 0.4945} = \sqrt{2940 \times 0.4945} = \sqrt{1453.8} \approx 38.1\text{ m s}^{-1}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Check limiting cases: with friction, \(v_{\max} (38.1\text{ m s}^{-1})\) is larger than the frictionless optimum speed (\(28.1\text{ m s}^{-1}\)), which is physically correct. Thus, the maximum speed is \(38.1\text{ m s}^{-1}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(38.1\text{ m s}^{-1}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWSOFMOTION_NUMERICAL_Q21 - Weighing scale reading in uniformly moving elevator

questiontext.text: A man of mass \(70\text{ kg}\) stands on a weighing scale in a lift. What is the reading on the scale (in newtons) when the lift moves upwards with a uniform speed of \(10\text{ m s}^{-1}\)? (Take \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of man: \(m = 70\text{ kg}\). Lift velocity: \(v = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}\) (constant, upwards). Acceleration: \(a = 0\text{ m s}^{-2}\). \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The reading on the scale equals the normal reaction force \(R\) exerted by the scale on the man.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Newton's second law for the man: \(R - mg = ma\). Since velocity is uniform, \(a = 0\), which gives \(R = mg\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given values: \(R = 70\text{ kg} \times 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2} = 686\text{ N}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
In an inertial frame moving at constant speed, true weight equals apparent weight. The scale reading is \(686\text{ N}\) (equivalent to \(70\text{ kg}\)).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(686\text{ N}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_LAWSOFMOTION_NUMERICAL_Q22 - Weighing scale reading in downward accelerating elevator

questiontext.text: A man of mass \(70\text{ kg}\) stands on a weighing scale in a lift. What is the reading on the scale (in newtons) when the lift accelerates downwards with a uniform acceleration of \(5\text{ m s}^{-2}\)? (Take \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\))

generalfeedback.text:
